purpose: Reference specification for AI-driven generation of new TOEFL ITP Level 1 practice items (Structure Part A, Written Expression Part B), derived from abstracted analysis of 200 official ETS TOEFL ITP items (Practice Tests B-F). Not intended to reproduce ETS source items.

source_data.note_practice_test_a: Practice Test A was not present in source materials and is not part of this analysis.

value_precedence: Where JSON/CSV source data (structure_items_all.json/.csv, written_expression_items_all.json/.csv) and Markdown analysis reports disagree, JSON/CSV is authoritative. All values in this file were computed directly from structure_items_all.json and written_expression_items_all.json.

primary_targets.definition: Whether an independent clause (subject + finite verb) is correctly formed; distinguishing fragments/run-ons; basic subject-verb agreement.
that-clauses and embedded/indirect questions functioning as subject, object, or complement; typically tests word order (no inversion) inside the clause.
Restrictive and non-restrictive relative clauses: relative pronoun choice/case, clause-internal parallelism, correct verb after the relative pronoun.
representative_subtypes: non-restrictive relative clause with parallel coordinate predicate
restrictive relative clause with correct relative pronoun

primary_targets.definition: Internal structure of time/cause/concession/condition/purpose subordinate clauses (full clause vs. phrase vs. inverted form). Use CONNECTORS_CONJUNCTIONS when the focus is choosing among connector words instead.
Choosing the correct linking word/phrase among conjunction/preposition/adverb options expressing cause, contrast, comparison, etc. (e.g. due to / because / in spite of / regardless of).
representative_subtypes: contrast connector selection (although vs. despite vs. however)

primary_targets.definition: Tense, aspect, and active/passive voice selection for the finite main verb of a clause. Use NONFINITE_VERB_PHRASES for participle/infinitive/gerund form selection.
representative_subtypes: past perfect vs. simple past selection
active vs. passive voice in main clause

primary_targets.definition: What correctly follows a linking verb (predicate nominative/adjective) or a causative/perception verb (object complement).
representative_subtypes: predicate nominative after linking verb (be + NP)
object complement after causative verb (make + O + Adj)

primary_targets.definition: Form selection for participles (reduced relative clauses, result participles), infinitives (purpose, modifying ordinal/superlative nouns), and gerunds.
representative_subtypes: reduced passive relative clause (past participle modifying noun)

primary_targets.definition: Comparative/superlative structures and degree constructions (enough, so, too, as...as).
Syntactic parallelism among elements joined by coordinating or correlative conjunctions (and, or, both...and, not only...but also) or in a list.
representative_subtypes: parallel verb forms in a list

primary_targets.definition: Internal word order of noun-modifying elements: adjective phrases, appositives, participial modifiers, noun phrase structure itself.
representative_subtypes: appositive noun phrase placement and internal word order
noun + postpositive adjective phrase word order
adjective order within a noun phrase

primary_targets.definition: Subject-auxiliary inversion triggered by fronted negative adverbials, place adverbials, or elliptical conditionals.
representative_subtypes: subject-auxiliary inversion after fronted negative adverbial ('Not until...')

primary_targets.definition: Expletive 'there + be' and 'it + be' constructions and the errors that arise from substituting a referring pronoun or bare determiner.
Pronoun-antecedent reference/agreement, articles, quantifiers (much/many, few/little, every/each), and countable/uncountable noun choice.

Which derivational/part-of-speech form of a word (adjective/adverb/noun/verb) a given syntactic slot requires - whether the slot is a noun-phrase-internal modifier, the head noun of a phrase, a verb-modifying adverbial, or a clause subject - when the error is not about element ordering (WORD_ORDER_MODIFICATION), required verb complementation (VERB_COMPLEMENTATION), or clause well-formedness (CLAUSE_STRUCTURE) as such. Added 2026-08-23; see GRAMMAR_TAXONOMY_CHANGELOG.md.
representative_subtypes: adjective required, adverb used to modify a following noun
adverb required, adjective/noun used to modify a verb
noun required, adjective used as clause subject
derivational noun-for-verb confusion as head of a prepositional-object phrase
ordinal number form required, cardinal used to modify a noun

tested_error_types.description: Incorrect tense/aspect/form (base/-ing/-ed etc.) of a verb.
A required element (subject, verb, connector, etc.) for the sentence/clause/phrase to be complete is missing.
An unnecessary or duplicated element is added.
All required elements are present but their order is wrong.
Wrong subordinating conjunction for the intended semantic/syntactic relation.
Wrong relative pronoun/marker choice or case (who/whom/which/that/whose).
Does not form a complete clause (missing finite verb or subject).
Subject is redundantly duplicated (e.g. relative pronoun plus a resumptive pronoun).
Subject-verb number agreement, or noun-quantifier agreement, error.
The complement structure (part of speech / phrase type) required by a linking or causative/perception verb is wrong. Does not cover fixed preposition collocations - see wrong_preposition_collocation.
The word's part of speech itself is wrong. Does not cover comparative/superlative confusion - see wrong_degree_form.
Pronoun has no clear or appropriate antecedent.

A fixed lexical preposition collocation governed by a verb/participle/adjective/noun is violated, or a standalone (non-governed) preposition/connector pairing is wrong (e.g. 'benefit from' vs 'benefit of', 'beside' vs 'between'). Not a part-of-speech error and not a clause-structural complementation mismatch - a lexical collocation slip. Added 2026-08-23; see GRAMMAR_TAXONOMY_CHANGELOG.md.

Comparative/superlative/positive degree confusion (e.g. superlative used where a comparative is required), or wrong degree/intensity marker for a construction that requires one (e.g. 'very' used where 'so' is required to license a following result clause). Added 2026-08-23; see GRAMMAR_TAXONOMY_CHANGELOG.md.

taxonomy_holdouts.note: Single-instance unresolved taxonomy holdouts (taxonomy_issue: true in source JSON). Do not create new generation categories based on these 3 items.
taxonomy_holdouts.reminder: These 3 items are not to be used as the basis for any new generation category. They remain single-instance, unresolved taxonomy edge cases (taxonomy_issue: true) and are noted here for completeness only.

observed: Exactly one choice restores a grammatically complete, standard-written-English sentence.
The other three choices are plausible grammatical confusions, not random word salad.
derived_rules: Generated items MUST have exactly 4 options and exactly 1 correct option.
The correct option must produce a complete, well-formed sentence with no residual grammar errors.
Distractors must be constructed from the observed error_type vocabulary (see distractor_design), not invented ad hoc.

sentence_length.derived_rule: Generated Structure items should normally fall within the observed 10-27 word range, concentrated around 15-24 words.
sentence_length.heuristic: For a batch: target a mean near 20 words with occasional short items (~10-14 words) and occasional long items (~25-27 words); do not make every item the same length.

clause_count.derived_rule: A generated batch's clause_count distribution should not deviate sharply from: roughly 1/3 single-clause, roughly half two-clause, a minority (10-15%) three-or-more-clause.
clause_count.heuristic: For a 15-item batch: approximately 5 items at 1 clause, 7-8 at 2 clauses, 2-3 at 3+ clauses.

primary_target_distribution.note: See top-level primary_targets[].structure_observed for authoritative counts/pct. generation_guidance_ranges below are HEURISTIC, not exact quotas.
primary_target_distribution.important: Do not treat observed percentage as a strict quota. A 0% observed category (WORD_CLASS_FORM) is not observed in this 75-item Structure sample but is not forbidden; Structure's item format may simply surface it rarely. Use sparingly (0-4% guidance) if used at all.

observed_error_type_distribution.note: wrong_preposition_collocation observed 0 times as a Structure distractor error_type in this sample; Written Expression surfaces it instead (see written_expression_spec). Not forbidden for Structure, just rare/unobserved.

distractor_design.derived_rule: Each distractor must be built using one of the 15 tested_error_type mechanisms from the shared taxonomy (grammar_taxonomy.json), favoring the four dominant mechanisms (missing_required_element, extraneous_element, wrong_word_order, fragment - together 64% of observed distractors) but not exclusively.
hard_requirements_per_distractor: Superficially plausible to a learner (uses real English words, not gibberish).
The grammatical difference from the correct answer must be explicitly describable in one sentence.
Must not create a second defensible correct answer.
Must not be eliminable by vocabulary knowledge alone (i.e., the flaw is grammatical/structural, not lexical rarity).

correct_answer_position.derived_rule: Over a large generated corpus, correct-answer position should trend toward roughly even across A-D.
correct_answer_position.heuristic: Do not force exactly 25% per option in every small batch; natural variance (as observed: 21.3%-28.0% range across 75 items) is acceptable and expected.

vocabulary_domain.derived_rule: Generated items should draw from a wide range of academic/general-interest domains (natural science, social science, history, art, humanities, geography, biography, technology, etc.), avoiding heavy repetition of any single domain within a batch.
vocabulary_domain.heuristic: No specific domain list is mandated - reproduce the observed diversity, not the observed domains themselves. Background/world knowledge must never be required to select the correct answer; all necessary information must be inferable from the sentence's own grammar.

estimated_difficulty_ai_1to5.note: 1 and 5 not observed; this is an AI structural estimate, NOT an ETS official difficulty rating

difficulty_characteristics.derived_rule: estimated_difficulty_ai must never be presented to end users or downstream systems as an official ETS difficulty score.
difficulty_characteristics.heuristic: Control generation difficulty via syntax complexity, clause nesting depth, distractor similarity, rarity of the tested construction, and distance between grammatically related elements - not via inserting harder vocabulary.

observed: Complete sentence with four marked/underlined portions (A-D).
Exactly one portion contains a grammatical error.
The other three portions are standard, acceptable written English.
derived_rules: Generated items MUST have exactly 4 marked portions and exactly 1 erroneous portion.
The 3 non-erroneous portions must be genuinely correct standard written English - not merely 'less wrong'.
Exactly one genuine grammatical error may exist in the sentence; no incidental second error is permitted anywhere in the sentence, marked or unmarked.

primary_target_distribution.important: 4 of 15 categories (NOUN_CLAUSES, ADVERBIAL_CLAUSES, INVERSION, EXISTENTIAL_EXPLETIVE) were not observed in this 125-item Written Expression sample. This reflects the item format (whole-clause/connector choices are Structure's domain; Written Expression tests word-level/local errors) more than a prohibition. Use sparingly (0-4% guidance) if used at all.

tested_error_type_distribution.note_fragment: fragment is observed 0 times in Written Expression because sentences are always presented complete by format definition - this is a structural impossibility for this section, not a sampling gap.
tested_error_type_distribution.note_new_types: wrong_preposition_collocation and wrong_degree_form were added to the taxonomy (v1.0 to v1.1) specifically because Written Expression items exposed real gaps; both are legitimate, well-evidenced generation targets, not edge cases.

representative_abstract_patterns.incorrect_part_of_speech: A word occupies a syntactic slot (modifier, head noun, subject, predicate complement) requiring one part of speech, but a different derivational form (adjective/adverb/noun/verb) is used.
representative_abstract_patterns.wrong_verb_form: Incorrect tense/aspect/base-form of a verb given the sentence's time-frame or surrounding auxiliary.
representative_abstract_patterns.agreement_error: Subject-verb number mismatch, or noun-quantifier mismatch (countable/uncountable).
representative_abstract_patterns.wrong_preposition_collocation: A fixed lexical preposition governed by a verb/adjective/participle/noun (or a standalone paired-preposition idiom) is swapped for a plausible but incorrect preposition.
representative_abstract_patterns.incorrect_relative_marker: Wrong relative pronoun choice or case (who/whom/which/that/whose) for the antecedent and clause role.
representative_abstract_patterns.extraneous_element: An unnecessary or duplicated word/phrase is inserted.
representative_abstract_patterns.missing_required_element: A required element for the phrase/clause to be complete is omitted.
representative_abstract_patterns.wrong_word_order: Required elements are present but incorrectly ordered.
representative_abstract_patterns.wrong_voice: Active/passive voice mismatch given the sentence's logical subject/object relationship.
representative_abstract_patterns.incorrect_reference: A pronoun's antecedent is missing, ambiguous, or mismatched in number/gender.
representative_abstract_patterns.incorrect_subordinator: Wrong subordinating conjunction for the intended semantic/syntactic relation.
representative_abstract_patterns.wrong_degree_form: Comparative/superlative/positive degree confusion, or wrong degree/intensity marker (e.g. very where so...that is required).
representative_abstract_patterns.double_subject: Subject redundantly duplicated (e.g. relative pronoun plus resumptive pronoun).

error_span_type_distribution.derived_rule: Generated batches should not concentrate error spans in one or two span_types; the observed top-4 (noun_phrase/verb_phrase/adjective/prepositional_phrase = 61.6%) is a reasonable center of mass but the long tail of 10 other span_types should also appear across a large batch.

observed_grammatical_role_of_dummy_spans.note: main_verb appears as a dummy span roughly 2x as often (15.7%) as it appears as the actual error span (8.0%) - correct main verbs are frequently used as plausible-looking non-errors.

derived_rules: All 4 marked portions must be natural candidates for grammatical scrutiny - a test-taker should be able to imagine each one being the error before reading closely.
The correct (erroneous) span should not be conspicuously longer or shorter than the 3 dummy spans.
The correct (erroneous) span should not be obviously strange in isolation - it must require reading in context to detect.
The 3 dummy spans should be positioned where a careful reader would plausibly want to double-check them (not filler words in trivial positions).

error_location_distribution.derived_rule: Randomize error location per item, but across a batch keep the overall shape similar to observed (slight skew toward late/sentence_final, sentence_initial least common) rather than clustering all errors in one position.

error_scope_distribution.difficulty_use: local errors are, in this dataset, associated with lower error_detectability values (easier to find) and cross_clause errors with higher values (harder), but this is a directional tendency observed in the data, not a strict, mechanically enforced rule - do not assume every cross_clause error is automatically hard or every local error automatically easy.

correct_answer_position.derived_rule: Over a large generated corpus, error position should trend toward even across A-D.
correct_answer_position.heuristic: The observed sample skews slightly light on A (19.2%) and heavy on B (29.6%); when generating large batches, lean slightly toward including more A-position errors than the raw observed ratio to avoid compounding this skew, without forcing exact 25% quotas on small batches.

sentence_and_clause_characteristics.derived_rule: Treat as a distribution independent from Structure's (Written Expression skews toward slightly simpler clause structure - single-clause and two-clause sentences are nearly tied, three+ clause sentences are rarer than in Structure).
sentence_and_clause_characteristics.heuristic: For a 25-item batch: roughly 11-12 single-clause, 11-12 two-clause, 1-2 three-clause sentences; mean sentence length near 20 words with occasional items up to ~30+ words.

error_detectability_1to5.note: 1=easy to find, 5=hard to find. No 5s observed in this sample.

estimated_difficulty_ai_1to5.note: AI structural estimate, NOT an ETS official difficulty rating.

difficulty_characteristics.derived_rule: estimated_difficulty_ai must never be presented as an official ETS difficulty score.
difficulty_characteristics.heuristic: Control difficulty via error_scope (local vs cross_clause), error_detectability-relevant surface cues, and distractor_plausibility of the 3 non-erroneous spans - not via obscure vocabulary.

vocabulary_domain.derived_rule: Generated Written Expression items should draw from a wide range of academic/general-interest domains, reproducing this observed diversity (a higher raw unique-domain count than Structure's, consistent with the larger 125-item batch size), not any specific observed domain list.
vocabulary_domain.heuristic: No specific domain list is mandated - reproduce the observed diversity, not the observed domains themselves. No single domain should be heavily overrepresented in a generated batch (the observed sample's most-repeated domain, art history, is still only 4.0% of items). Background/world knowledge must never be required to correct the erroneous portion; the flaw must be locatable using only the sentence's own grammar.

difficulty_framework.status: HEURISTIC - shared across Structure and Written Expression, informed by but not a fixed conversion of estimated_difficulty_ai (1-5)
factors: structural dependency distance (how far apart the grammatically related elements are)
error_scope (Written Expression: local vs clause_level vs sentence_level vs cross_clause)
difficulty_framework.explicit_non_factor: Vocabulary specialization/rarity alone must NOT be used to raise difficulty; difficulty must come from grammar/syntax, not lexis.
difficulty_framework.note_on_ai_estimate_mapping: estimated_difficulty_ai (1-5) is not converted to EASY/MEDIUM/HARD by a fixed formula. As an approximate reference only: Structure's observed estimated_difficulty_ai distribution (2=24%, 3=56%, 4=20%; no 1s or 5s observed) and Written Expression's (1=14.4%, 2=48.8%, 3=29.6%, 4=7.2%; no 5s observed) suggest that most official items cluster in the low-to-mid range of the 1-5 scale, and 'HARD' generated items should still usually resemble the observed 4-tier ceiling rather than inventing more extreme difficulty than ETS itself produced in this sample.

shared: Exactly four options / four marked portions per item.
Exactly one intended correct answer / one intended erroneous portion.
The answer must be defensible by standard written English grammar rules, unambiguously.
No specialized factual/world knowledge may be required to answer correctly.
Avoid semantic ambiguity that could create multiple acceptable answers.
Difficulty must primarily come from grammar/syntax, not vocabulary difficulty.
Do not reproduce or lightly paraphrase any ETS source item from the 200-item analyzed set.
Do not reuse distinctive proper nouns, numerical facts, or unusual wording found in source items.
Do not make the correct answer systematically the longest or most elaborately worded option.
Do not introduce unintended secondary grammatical errors anywhere in the item.
structure_specific: The blank, once filled with the correct option, must produce one complete, grammatically well-formed sentence with no other errors.
All three distractors must be constructible back to one of the 15 tested_error_type mechanisms in grammar_taxonomy.json.
Do not use a distractor that is correct in one plausible reading of the sentence (no accidental double-correct answers).
Sentence must stand alone (no external context/passage required).
written_expression_specific: The sentence, once the erroneous portion is corrected, must be entirely free of grammatical errors.
Exactly one of the four marked portions may be grammatically wrong; the other three must be independently, unambiguously correct.
The erroneous portion's flaw must be locatable and correctable using only information inside the sentence.
Do not mark a portion as an error if fixing it would leave the sentence still containing a different genuine error elsewhere.

anti_patterns: Obviously broken / nonsensical distractors that no test-taker would plausibly select.
Two options that are both independently defensible as correct.
Testing obscure vocabulary knowledge rather than grammar knowledge.
Conversational or informal sentence register (TOEFL ITP style is formal/academic).
Unnatural, gibberish-sounding academic prose assembled just to hit a word count.
Every item in a batch having near-identical sentence length.
Every HARD item using the same construction (e.g. always inversion).
Correct answers concentrated in only B/C across a batch, systematically avoiding A/D.
A Written Expression sentence containing two genuine grammatical errors (only one may be intended).
An underlined/marked error identifiable without reading the rest of the sentence (i.e., detectable in isolation).
Distractors that differ from the correct answer only by random word-order scrambling with no coherent pedagogical rationale (i.e., not tied to a real error_type mechanism).
Reusing a source item's distinctive subject matter, named entity, date, or statistic even when the wording is changed.

batch_level_diversity_controls: primary_target diversity - spread across multiple categories per batch, informed by the generation_guidance_ranges_pct, not a single repeated category.
answer-position balance - avoid systematic skew toward any one of A-D across the batch.
sentence-length diversity - mix of short/medium/long items per the observed distribution shape.
clause-count diversity - mix of 1/2/3+ clause items per the observed distribution shape.
topic/vocabulary-domain diversity - avoid repeating the same domain more than 1-2 times in a batch.
difficulty diversity - a mix of EASY/MEDIUM/HARD per the difficulty_framework, not all-same-difficulty.
error-type diversity (tested_error_type / distractor error_type) - spread across multiple mechanisms, favoring but not limited to the dominant observed ones.
batch_generation_blueprint.explicit_non_goal: Do not attempt to exactly reproduce the observed 75-item / 125-item distributions in every batch. Reasonable variance from batch to batch is expected and desirable; the observed distributions are a center of gravity, not a checklist to tick off per batch.

example_difficulty_split_structure_15_it.derivation: HEURISTIC, proportional to observed estimated_difficulty_ai tiers (2=24%, 3=56%, 4=20%) applied to a 15-item batch.

example_difficulty_split_written_express.derivation: HEURISTIC, proportional to observed estimated_difficulty_ai tiers (1+2=63.2% -> EASY, 3=29.6% -> MEDIUM, 4=7.2% -> HARD) applied to a 25-item batch.

copyright_and_source_separation.principle: This specification describes abstract item-design features distilled from ETS TOEFL ITP items. It does not itself contain, quote, or closely paraphrase ETS item text.
generator_constraints: Do not copy sentences or sentence fragments from any of the 200 analyzed source items.
Do not lightly paraphrase (synonym-swap) a source item while preserving its structure/content.
Do not reuse distinctive phrases, named entities, dates, or statistics from source items.
Do not reproduce the same combination of person + fact + number found in a source item, even with different wording.
Every generated item must be an independently authored sentence built from this specification's abstracted design features, not derived from any specific source item.

machine_readable_constraints_summary.note: This is a compressed cross-reference only. Authoritative detail lives in structure_spec / written_expression_spec / hard_rules / difficulty_framework above - do not treat this summary as a replacement for those sections.
